correctness.rationale: The local degree bound gives the path, ray, line, and cycle component split. On a source-rooted path, induction shows that precisely the even-distance vertices enter, one additional even-distance vertex per stage; a finite path stabilizes after the ceiling of half its vertices. Source-free components remain empty by transfinite induction. In the effective class, predecessor iteration enumerates the grounded extension; a finite grounding ordinal supplies a fixed finite search bound. The uniform construction has computable neighbor functions, degree at most one, a grounded set coding the chosen c.e. set across copies, and unbounded finite path lengths, so it realizes every c.e. degree at the first infinite grounding ordinal.

value.rationale: The simultaneous in-degree/out-degree-one restriction is a natural sparse boundary class. The result is a complete structural classification and a sharp stage/degree boundary: finite grounding depth forces a computable grounded set, while behavior requiring arbitrarily late finite stages realizes every c.e. degree without branching. This identifies the exact computability-theoretic capacity of a minimal local interaction structure rather than reporting a routine finite example.
